newsitem.title: USA: US Treasuries in choppy, narrow-range trade Wed.
newsitem.headline: US Treasuries in choppy, narrow-range trade Wed.

text.p: The prices of U.S. Treasury securities opened in choppy trading Wednesday following a policy-makers remarks and a weak housing starts report.

U.S. housing starts fell 12.2 percent in December to a 1.329 million annual rate and permits fell 0.6 percent to a 1.410 million annual rate. Economists surveyed by Reuters expected that housing starts for December would show an average rate of 1.470 million versus 1.514 million the prior month.
The long bond was down 2/32 at 96-9/32 to yield 6.79 percent.
Comments by Federal Reserve Board Governor Susan Phillips took the wind out of overnight gains Wednesday shortly before the release of housing starts data.

Phillips told a news wire she might not be willing to wait for an uptick in core consumer prices before calling for a tightening; that a taut labor market contained risk of wage inflation and that capacity utilization was a concern to the Fed.
The remarks seemed to contradict the more balanced and temperate tone of Fed Chairman Alan Greenspan's speech before the Senate Budget Committee on Tuesday.
Market tone remained positive overnight in Europe following Greenspan's speech that seemed to preclude a tightening of monetary policy when the Fed next meets on February 4 and 5.

"Phillips saying she might not want to wait to see inflation before moving took the market down, but the dollar is strong; we saw a lot of international buying and Greenspan's comments still provided a lot of relief," said Mead Briggs, proprietary trading manager at Credit Suisse First Boston.
The Treasury willl auction $17.5 billion of two-year notes at 1300 EST/1800 GMT.
"We expect to see a lot of short bases building before the auction today," a trader at a primary dealership said.

"Greenspan seemed to indicate no tightening in February. He didn't rule out anything after that, but the next meeting isn't until March 25 and this is a day-to-day business," the trader said. "That's a world of time away."
The trader pointed out that it's still just the beginning of the year and Treasury yields at current levels were attractive to many investors.
"And, with the stock market at the highs it's at a lot of people are afraid of stocks," he said.
The Federal Reserve will release its Beige Book report of regional economic conditions at 1400 EST/1900 GMT.
The two-year note was at 99-20/32, unchanged to yield 5.96 percent. The five-year was down 1/32 at 99-9/32 to yield 6.30 percent and the 10-year off 2/32 at 99-27/32 to yield 6.52 percent.
Three-month bill rates were unchanged at 5.03 percent. Six-month rates were up 1/32 at 5.11 percent and year bill rates were unchanged at 5.28 percent.
